newsitem.title: UK: Norway unlikely to privatise Statoil - chief exec.
newsitem.headline: Norway unlikely to privatise Statoil - chief exec.

text.p: Privatisation of Norway's state-owned oil company, Den Norske Stats Oljeselskap AS (Statoil), is unlikely in the foreseeable future, Statoil's president and chief executive officer Harald Norvik said on Thursday.

"This issue will always be on the agenda but I see no majority in Norway for privatising Statoil," Norvik told a meeting of the Norwegian British Chamber of Commerce at the Institute of Directors to mark the opening of a new headquarters for Statoil (U.K.) Ltd.
Norvik said Statoil enjoyed a "very good" relationship with the government, adding that the Norwegian concept of public ownership was very positive.

"I think the question is not who the owner is but how the owner acts and relates to the company," he said, briefing an audience on Statoil's future strategy, which includes doubling equity hydrocarbon production to one million barrels of oil equivalent by 2005.
